title: Push and pull: why people migrate
examples: What are push and pull factors?
What is the difference between a migrant and a refugee?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Does it push people away or pull them in?

explain.say: Imagine your family packs up and moves to a new country. Why would anyone leave home? Migration means moving to live in a new place. Look at the board. Geographers sort the reasons into push factors, which drive people away, and pull factors, which draw them somewhere new.

draw.text: Push and pull: why people migrate

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does it push people away or pull them in?

explain.say: Look at the push factors. War, drought, floods and having no work can push people out of their homes. Millions of Syrians fled the war that began in 2011, many to Türkiye. What might push a family to leave?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does it push people away or pull them in?

explain.say: Now the pull factors. Better-paid jobs, safety, good schools, hospitals and family already living there pull people in. Millions of workers from India, Nepal and the Philippines go to Gulf countries like the United Arab Emirates for work. Which pull would matter most to you?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does it push people away or pull them in?

explain.say: But moving is not easy. See the obstacles: visas and borders, the cost of the journey and learning a new language. Many people move inside their own country instead, from a village to a city, as millions do in China and India. Is it easier to move within a country or to another one?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Does it push people away or pull them in?

explain.say: So people migrate when push and pull are strong enough to beat the obstacles. Great sorting! Wow fact: about 280 million people, roughly 1 in every 30 people on Earth, live outside the country where they were born.

faq.a: Push factors are things that make people want to leave a place, such as war, persecution, natural disasters, drought, unemployment and poverty.
asks: Why do people leave their country?
What are push and pull factors?

faq.a: Pull factors are things that attract people to a new place, such as jobs, higher wages, safety, schools, health care and family members who already live there.
asks: Why do people move to cities?

faq.a: Obstacles such as borders and visas, the cost and danger of the journey, distance, a new language and leaving family behind. Geographers call these intervening obstacles.

faq.q: What is the difference between a migrant and a refugee?
faq.a: A migrant is anyone who moves to live in another place, for any reason. A refugee has been forced to flee their country because of war or persecution, and is protected by international law.

faq.q: How many people live outside their birth country?
faq.a: About 281 million people in 2020, roughly 3.6 percent of the world, according to the UN. India has the most people living abroad, about 18 million.
asks: Which country has the most people living abroad?

facts: About 281 million people, about 3.6% of the world, lived outside their country of birth in 2020 (UN DESA).
India has the largest number of emigrants of any country, about 18 million.
Most of the United Arab Emirates' residents were born in other countries.

quiz.why: Better-paid jobs attract people to a new place, so they are a pull factor.

wrong.1: A drought drives people away, so it is a push factor.
wrong.2: A war drives people away, so it is a push factor.
